correctness.rationale: Exact inclusion-exclusion P(T>k)=nq^k−Σp_e^k for k>=1. Equal degree constraints become fractional 1-factors of K_n. At an extreme point every support component is isolated weight-one K2 or weight-half odd cycle; proof derives this from unsigned incidence-column independence, degree counts, and alternating even-cycle null vectors. Strict convexity of sum w_e^k for k>=2 and minimal cycle vertices (0 for even n; 3 for odd n) yield lower tail bound with uniqueness; Jensen yields upper with unique equality. Explicit geometric series establish means. Analytic proof covers all integers n>=4,k>=1 and real feasible masses; 384 exact-rational checks including independent direct sample enumeration support reproducibility, not replace proof.

originality.rationale: Compared exact law and parameter domain to primary full-text group-drawing literature, a classical half-package stochastic-optimality theorem, more general balanced coverage bounds, and available mathematical-record and historical claims. None of the examined statements entails both sharp finite-time extrema over all balanced n-2 package laws with odd-n triangle and uniqueness. The known n=4 special case is not claimed as novel; unresolved risk from unavailable 2021 full text and potentially unindexed earlier results remains.
residual_risks: Full 2021 Schilling article could not be obtained; its abstract was available and refers to expectations only.
An unindexed classical fractional-matching power-sum extremum could imply the classification, notwithstanding absence from searched records.

value.rationale: The equal-individual-marginal fairness constraint makes differences in completion-time laws depend solely on higher-order omissions. The result determines the entire sharp first-order stochastic-dominance interval over this natural full-dimensional constrained design class, all horizons and sharp means; it also classifies all extremizers with a parity-sensitive triangle obstruction. This is a significant structural classification rather than a routine bound or arbitrarily chosen small parameter and is not implied by the previously proved unrestricted-mean improvement; the n=4 covered case is acknowledged rather than claimed as new.
